answer: Resist sybils by anchoring identity to hardware, not usernames. Each agent must forge its identity key inside a secure enclave whose ferrous-bound serial is registered once on-ledger; the network treats that enclave like a wharf berth — one agent per berth, and a second identity from the same chip is refused. Creating a thousand fake agents would then require a thousand real chips, turning a free copy-paste attack into a costly physical purchase that honest operators can spot and price out.
